instructions:
You build a library of GMP audit checklist requirements. You get the requirements the library already has and a
list of obligations drafted from one regulator's texts. Decide, for every obligation, which requirement it
belongs to. Your output is checked by software and by independent reviewers.

A requirement is ONE auditable point, written for a checklist (for example "Self-inspections are carried out
at planned intervals under a written programme"). Several regulators state the same point in different words;
they share one requirement. Do not merge two different points into one requirement, and do not split one point.

For each obligation give exactly one decision:
- requirement: the id of an existing requirement (as listed, e.g. "SI-004") when the obligation states that
  point, or a new key "NEW-1", "NEW-2", ... when no listed requirement states it. Several obligations of this
  list may use the same new key when they state the same new point. Define each new key once, on its first use.
- relation of the obligation to the requirement's text:
  - "same": it states the point, no stricter and no wider.
  - "stricter": it states the point but demands more (a fixed frequency, a shorter time, a stronger verb).
  - "adds": it states the point and adds a further element (another condition, record, person or content).
  - "looser": it states the point but demands less (a weaker verb such as "may", fewer elements).
  - "narrower": it states the point only for a narrower scope (one product type, one activity, one case).
  The first use of a new key is always "same": its item_text is written from that obligation.
- addendum: for "stricter" and "adds", one short plain-English sentence with only what this regulator demands
  beyond the requirement's text (e.g. "At least once a year."). It is shown to the customer appended to the
  requirement text, so it must read well on its own. Empty for the other relations.
- topic: for the first use of a new key, the sub-topic id from the topic list that the point belongs to;
  empty otherwise.
- item_text: for the first use of a new key, the requirement in your own plain English words, as one checklist
  item a site can be audited against, keeping every condition and number of the obligation. Empty otherwise.
- reason: one short sentence on why.

Rules for every text you write (item_text and addendum):
- Use your own words. Never copy 12 or more words in a row from the obligation's quote, and avoid copying
  shorter runs of the regulator's wording.
- No clause numbers, document names, regulator names, section signs or references ("as in 9.2", "Annex 1").
- Do not add anything the obligation does not say.
- A condition the obligation states ("where an audit is required", "before approval") must be in the text that
  the customer sees: in item_text for a new requirement, or in the addendum (relation "adds") when the existing
  requirement's text lacks it.

Judge only from the texts given. Answer with one decision per obligation, in the order given.

REQUIREMENTS SO FAR:
PER-001 [PER.ORG] (recommended; API) The core duties of the independent quality unit are kept by that unit and are not handed over to others.
PER-002 [PER.ORG] (recommended; API) The duties of the quality unit are set out in writing and cover at least the minimum set of quality responsibilities.
REL-001 [REL.REVIEW] (recommended; API) The quality unit decides on release or rejection of every active substance, and of any intermediate intended for use outside the manufacturer's control.
MAT-001 [MAT.STATUS] (recommended; API) The quality unit has set up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, and packaging and labelling materials.
REL-002 [REL.REVIEW] (recommended; API) Before an active substance is released for distribution, the quality unit reviews the completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps.
QS-001 [QS.DEV] (recommended; API) The quality unit makes sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved.
DOC-001 [DOC.SPEC] (recommended; API) The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.
DOC-002 [DOC.SOP] (recommended; API) The quality unit approves every procedure that can affect the quality of intermediates or active substances.
SI-001 [SI.PROG] (recommended; API) The quality unit makes sure that internal audits (self-inspections) take place.
OUT-001 [OUT.CONTRACT] (recommended; API) The quality unit approves the contract manufacturers used for intermediates and active substances.
QS-002 [QS.CHANGE] (recommended; API) The quality unit approves any change that might affect the quality of an intermediate or active substance.
VAL-001 [VAL.PLAN] (recommended; API) The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and validation reports.
CMP-001 [CMP.COMPL] (recommended; API) The quality unit makes sure that quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.
EQ-001 [EQ.MAINT] (recommended; API) The quality unit makes sure that effective systems are in use for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment.
QC-001 [QC.TEST] (recommended; API) The quality unit makes sure that materials are suitably tested and that the results are reported.
QC-002 [QC.STAB] (recommended; API) Where appropriate, the quality unit makes sure that stability data exist to support the retest or expiry dates and storage conditions of active substances and/or intermediates.
QS-003 [QS.PQR] (recommended; API) The quality unit carries out product quality reviews.
SI-002 [SI.PROG] (mandatory; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out regularly, following an approved schedule, to check compliance with GMP.
SI-003 [SI.REPORT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Findings from internal audits and the related corrective actions are documented and brought to the attention of the company's responsible management.
SI-004 [SI.FOLLOW] (mandatory; API) Corrective actions agreed after internal audits are completed on time and effectively.
MAT-002 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether an effective pharmaceutical quality system has been set up and put into practice.
MAT-003 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there are enough competent and suitably qualified staff.
MAT-004 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether managerial and supervisory staff responsible for manufacturing and quality activities have defined job descriptions.
MAT-005 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there are training programmes on health, hygiene and clothing where the intended operations need them.
MAT-006 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether premises and equipment suited to the intended operations are provided and maintained.
MAT-007 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether documentation systems cover all processes and specifications for the manufacturing and quality operations.
MAT-008 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether starting materials, intermediates and excipients are coded and identified so that they are fully traceable.
MAT-009 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there is a programme for qualifying suppliers.
MAT-010 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there is a quality control system for the excipient and a responsible person, independent of production, who releases batches.
MAT-011 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether records of incoming materials and excipients, and samples of excipients, are kept for the required retention periods.
MAT-012 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there are systems ensuring that every outsourced activity is covered by a written contract.
MAT-013 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether an effective system is maintained for reviewing complaints and recalling excipients.
MAT-014 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether there is a system for managing changes and deviations.
MAT-015 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether environmental control and storage conditions are in place.
SI-005 [SI.TEAM] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspections are carried out in an independent and thorough way by designated, competent staff of the company.
SI-006 [SI.TEAM] (optional; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Independent audits by external experts may be used in addition to self-inspections.
SI-007 [SI.REPORT] (mandatory; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) A record is kept of every self-inspection.
SI-008 [SI.REPORT] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspection reports contain all observations made and, where applicable, proposed corrective measures.
QS-004 [QS.PQS] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The manufacturer takes the applicable GMP guidelines into account so that GMP principles are applied consistently.
QS-005 [QS.PQS] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) For advanced therapy medicinal products, the GMP guideline specific to those products is applied.
MAT-016 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether everyone working in manufacturing and quality activities is covered by a training programme.
QS-006 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The quality system is designed, planned, put in place, maintained and continually improved so that products with suitable quality attributes are delivered consistently.
QS-007 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Knowledge of the product and the process is managed at every stage of the lifecycle.
QS-008 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Medicinal products are designed and developed with GMP requirements taken into account.
QS-009 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Production and control operations are clearly defined and carried out under GMP.
QS-010 [QS.MGMT] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Management responsibilities are clearly defined.
MAT-017 [MAT.SUPP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Arrangements are in place for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for choosing and monitoring suppliers, and for checking that every delivery comes from the approved supply chain.
OUT-002 [OUT.CONTRACT] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Processes are in place for managing outsourced activities.
QS-011 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Process performance and product quality are monitored and controlled through effective systems that bring about and keep a state of control.
QS-012 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Results from monitoring products and processes are used in batch release, in deviation investigations and for preventive action to avoid future deviations.
PROD-001 [PROD.IPC] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Every necessary check on intermediate products, together with other in-process controls and validations, is performed.
QS-013 [QS.PQS] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Quality improvements suited to the current level of process and product knowledge are put in place to support continual improvement.
QS-014 [QS.CHANGE] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before they are implemented, with regulatory notification and approval taken into account where required.
QS-015 [QS.CHANGE] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) After a change is implemented, it is evaluated to confirm that its quality objectives were met and that product quality was not unintentionally harmed.
QS-016 [QS.DEV] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Investigations of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems use a suitable depth of root cause analysis.
QS-017 [QS.DEV] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) When the true root cause of a problem cannot be determined, the most likely root cause or causes are identified and addressed.
QS-018 [QS.DEV] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) A conclusion that human error caused a problem, whether suspected or confirmed, is justified only after confirming that no process, procedural or system-based errors or problems were missed.
QS-019 [QS.CAPA] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Suitable corrective and/or preventive actions are identified and taken in response to investigations.
QS-020 [QS.CAPA] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.
REL-003 [REL.QP] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) No medicinal product is sold or supplied until the certifying person (Qualified Person or Authorised Person) has certified that each production batch was made and controlled in line with the marketing authorisation and any other rules on production, control and release.
DIST-001 [DIST.STORE] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Arrangements are in place to make sure, as far as possible, that medicinal products are stored, distributed and handled afterwards in a way that keeps their quality throughout their shelf life.
SI-009 [SI.PROG] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises how effective and applicable the quality system is.

QS-022 [QS.PQR] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Management procedures are in place for the ongoing management and review of actions arising from the product quality review.
QS-023 [QS.PQR] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspection verifies the effectiveness of the procedures for managing and reviewing actions arising from the product quality review.
QS-024 [QS.PQR] (optional; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Where scientifically justified, product quality reviews may be grouped by product type, for example solid, liquid or sterile dosage forms.
QS-025 [QS.PQR] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement sets out each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.
CMP-002 [CMP.RECALL] (optional; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Besides recall, other actions to reduce the risk from quality defects may be considered, such as warning healthcare professionals about the use of a batch that may be defective.
CMP-003 [CMP.RECALL] (recommended; INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Risk-reducing actions other than recall are judged case by case and discussed with the competent authorities concerned.
CSV-001 [CSV.DI] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The data governance system applies controls across the whole data lifecycle that are proportionate to quality risk.
CSV-002 [CSV.DI] (optional; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Data lifecycle controls may combine organisational measures (record completion and retention procedures, staff training and documented authority to generate and approve data, a governance design that controls risks in how data are generated, recorded, processed, kept and used, routine daily, batch or activity checks of data, periodic surveillance such as self-inspection, and staff skilled in data integrity and security) with technical measures (validation, qualification and control of computerised systems, automation, or technologies that give tighter control of data).
CSV-003 [CSV.DI] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The effectiveness of data integrity controls is assessed periodically, through self-inspection or another periodic review, to confirm that data lifecycle controls work as intended.
SI-010 [SI.PROG] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Beyond routine data checks (daily, per batch or per activity), self-inspections take a wider look at data controls, including whether staff still understand good data management as a way of protecting patients and whether the workplace stays focused on quality with open reporting of problems, for example by reviewing ongoing data management training.
SI-011 [SI.PROG] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspections compare reported data and results with the raw entries, looking at data not covered by routine checks where risk justifies it and/or at a sample of data already checked, to confirm the routine check still works.
CSV-004 [CSV.AUDIT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspections examine a risk-based sample of computerised system logs and audit trails to confirm that GMP or GDP relevant information is reported correctly, especially where routine system data are reviewed by hand or through a validated exception report.
SI-012 [SI.PROG] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Self-inspections include a review of trends in quality system metrics, which may also show how effective data governance is.
CSV-005 [CSV.DI] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The quality system is able to prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in systems or processes that could lead to data integrity failures.
CSV-006 [CSV.DI] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The company understands its data lifecycle and builds in suitable controls and procedures so that the data it generates are valid, complete and reliable.
CSV-007 [CSV.DI] (optional; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Control and procedure changes for data integrity may cover quality risk management, investigations, data review practice, computerised system validation, physical and virtual IT infrastructure, services and security, vendor and contractor management, training on the company's data governance approach and procedures, storage, processing, transfer and retrieval of completed records (including decentralised or cloud-based activities), oversight of buying GMP or GDP critical equipment and IT with data integrity requirements such as user requirement specifications, a self-inspection programme that includes data quality and integrity, and quality metrics reported to senior management.
CSV-008 [CSV.DI] (optional; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Where summary data are passed between sites of the same organisation, the supplying site's compliance may be evaluated by other means, such as evidence that corporate procedures are followed or internal audit reports.
CSV-009 [CSV.AUDIT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) The quality unit sets up a programme and schedule for ongoing audit trail reviews, based on criticality and system complexity, to confirm current controls are working and to detect possible non-compliance.
CSV-010 [CSV.AUDIT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Audit trail reviews form part of the company's self-inspection programme.
CSV-011 [CSV.AUDIT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Procedures are in place to deal with and investigate any audit trail discrepancy, including escalation to senior management and to national authorities where necessary.
CSV-012 [CSV.AUDIT] (recommended; API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI) Audit trail reviews use both random selections and selections targeted by criticality or risk.
